subject: Siemic adapter onboarding — compatibility questions & proposed next steps
messages:
From: Anya Kozlova <anya@siemic.ai>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 18 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Siemic adapter onboarding: compatibility notes and questions

Hi Irene —

Thanks again for taking the call yesterday. Attaching our current connector spec (siemic_connector_spec.pdf) — a short summary of the technical asks and the items that are blocking our marketplace listing: 

1) Entitlement tagging: our integration requires the marketplace to pass an entitlement flag in the provisioning webhook so we can enable advanced features.
2) OAuth flow: the marketplace sandbox uses a different redirect URI pattern from your hosted flow; we need clarity on allowed redirect URIs for embedded listing flows.
3) Private deployments: a handful of customers require IP allowlist and VPC peering; we need guidance on Private deployment network handoff and any dedicated capacity options.
4) Dedicated scaling: some enterprise customers want a guaranteed throughput SLA for our connector; we want to know if Redwood will support low-latency dedicated pools for ISV connectors on day one of listing.

Could you confirm which of the above Redwood can support out-of-the-box vs which would require an exemption or product change? Also, do you have an integration guide for the marketplace onboarding timeline and procurement path (contract & entitlements)?

Thanks — happy to hop on a 30m call if that's easier.

Best,
Anya
Partnerships, Siemic Solutions

Hi Anya —

Thanks for the spec — and for outlining the blockers so clearly. We're reviewing internally but wanted to confirm receipt and propose next steps: 

- Short answer: we can support the entitlement webhook and marketplace redirect patterns with a small integration shim; OAuth redirect URIs will need a short product clarification.
- Dedicated capacity / low-latency pools: possible but requires a reserved capacity commitment and an operational onboarding runbook (network + entitlements).
- IP allowlist / VPC peering for Private: supported via our Private offering but it does require an ops checklist and can be staged in a pre-prod sandbox first.

Internal ask: I'm looping in Karthik (product) for API surface confirmation, Marcus (platform partnerships/ops) for Dedicated/Private feasibility and ramp, and Monica (sales) to capture commercial/procurement expectations from Siemic customers.

Can we set a short working session this week to align on which items require a product change vs an integration playbook / exemption? I can host Tuesday 10–11 PT or Wednesday 2–3 PT.

Irene
Senior Partner Solutions

Team —

Summary of partner asks (see attached siemic_connector_spec.pdf and draft_mutual_action_plan.xlsx):

- Entitlement webhook and marketplace provisioning flag: partner expects the marketplace to pass a feature_entitlement=true flag on provisioning. Is that currently emitted by our provisioning webhook? If not, can we add a 1-field toggle? (low-effort ideally)
- OAuth redirect patterns: partner's sandbox uses /oauth/callback/siemic/*; need to confirm whether our listing flow allows wildcard redirect URIs or we must register specific URIs.
- Dedicated capacity request: they want a day-one option for a dedicated GPU pool for their top 10 enterprise customers. We need to be explicit on what "dedicated for an ISV connector" means operationally and on the pricing/commit needed.
- Private/VPC handoff: they will require IP allowlist and a way to exchange routing details — ops-runbook needed.

Immediate asks from each of you: 
- Karthik: product decision on entitlement webhook and whether we can accept a small compatibility shim in the runtime (or if it needs a product rollout). ETA?
- Marcus: ops feasibility for a pre-prod dedicated canary + Private handoff checklist. Any blockers for IP allowlist + VPC peering?
- Monica: commercial perspective — what procurement signals or commitment thresholds should we require before provisioning dedicated pools to an ISV?

Goal: come back with clear yes/no/needs-exemption for each bullet so I can respond to Siemic and propose either a standard integration path or an exemption + timeline.

Irene

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>

Date: Mon, 19 Oct 2026 13:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Internal: Siemic onboarding — quick alignment and asks (see attachments)

Thanks Irene. Quick responses from product side: 

- Entitlement webhook: we do not currently send a freeform feature_entitlement flag in the provisioning webhook. We can add a small optional field (feature_entitlements: [string]) without runtime changes to inference. This is a low-risk change — estimate 1 sprint (2 weeks) including tests and docs.
- OAuth redirect URIs: our marketplace onboarding requires exact-match redirect registration for security reasons; we cannot accept wildcards in prod. We can support adding partner sandbox URIs to the allowed list on a per-listing basis. That is an Ops/Console change (manual registration) but not a product-level runtime change.
- Dedicated pools: product is okay with supporting ISV-dedicated pools but it should be behind a reserved-capacity product offering (Dedicated/ISV SKU). We should not create ad-hoc infra exceptions without a commercial commit.

Proposed path:
1) Add the optional entitlement field (INF-4821). I will create the Jira ticket and provide a PR for review; target ship: 2 weeks.
2) For OAuth patterns, register the sandbox redirect URIs during onboarding (manual ops step).
3) For dedicated pools, require a minimum 3-month reserved commit; Marcus to confirm operational onboarding and pricing.

I'll link the Jira and a short spec doc here.

Karthik
Product — Integrations

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Internal: Siemic onboarding — ops constraints & recommended path

Thanks — operational notes from my side: 

- Pre-prod sandbox: preferred path is to run Siemic's connector in our ISV sandbox with an ops-runbook (ops_runbook.md) and full ingress/egress tests. This avoids immediate Dedicated provisioning while we validate scale.
- IP allowlist / VPC peering: supported but requires a signed data transfer addendum and network runbook; lead time ~2 weeks once we have customer routing details.
- Dedicated canary: we can spin a short-lived dedicated pool (canary) for compatibility testing for up to 2 weeks at no charge if it's purely for integration validation. Any long-running dedicated capacity requires a reserved commit (3 months minimum).

Next steps I propose:
- Offer Siemic a 2-week integration canary in our sandbox and manual registration of their sandbox redirect URIs.
- Karthik to track the entitlement field work (INF-4821) and ship in the 2-week window.
- Monica to capture commercial commitment language for Dedicated/ISV SKU.

I'll attach a short ops checklist and can run the initial canary onboarding with Siemic next week if we have alignment.

Marcus
Platform Partnerships / Ops
